summary.plain: XENON1T was a tank of liquid xenon deep under a mountain in Italy that searched for dark matter particles bumping into xenon atoms. It ran from 2015 to 2018 and was for a time the most sensitive dark matter detector in the world. It is the direct predecessor of the larger XENONnT experiment now running in the same underground hall.
summary.technical: First tonne-scale dual-phase xenon TPC dark matter search: 3.2 t total / 2.0 t active liquid xenon, built 2014-2015 and operated 2015-2018 in LNGS Hall B (~1400 m rock). Its first-results run (34.2 live days, Nov 2016 - Jan 2017) set a spin-independent WIMP-nucleon limit of 7.7 × 10⁻⁴⁷ cm² at 35 GeV/c². A 2020 analysis of low-energy electronic-recoil data reported an unexplained excess near 2-3 keV (tritium/axion/neutrino-magnetic-moment hypotheses considered, none confirmed). Stopped Dec 2018 to be upgraded into XENONnT.
